verdict.rationale: Fivetran's own MCP server can report per-connection sync status, such as whether the last sync succeeded or a connection is broken, and the docs have a "Fivetran Alerts" page, but that page is only a title with no detail on how alerts are delivered. The webhooks evidence concerns usage tracking for a source endpoint, not outbound failure alerts, so it earns no credit. missing for 10: sync logs, per-sync row counts, documented failure alert delivery to Slack, email, or webhook, dashboard run-history documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I see run status, logs, and row counts per sync, and failures alert me in Slack, email, or a webhook

citations.quote: It lets you ask questions like "was my last postgres sync successful" and "are any of my connections broken" and have the model answer the questions for you.
It allows you to ask read-only questions like "when was the last time my postgres connection completed a sync?" and "are any of my connections broken?"
